raw_record.question_text:
Read the contour topographic map of a certain area.

<image1>

The river section between A and C of this river has ice flood phenomena every spring. Write, in alphabetical order, the name of the second river bank where the river's sediment deposition is relatively significant: ____.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: a contour map with latitude 50°N marked, the river reach AC, and banks labeled D、E、F、B. Use the text clue that AC has spring ice floods to infer the river flows from the lower-latitude end C toward the higher-latitude end A. Then, facing downstream from C to A, mark the left banks along the reach. The labeled left banks are D and E, so when ordered alphabetically the second depositional bank is E岸.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一幅等高线地形图，顶部标有经度68°，右侧标有纬度50°N；图中有一条较粗的河流河段，标出A、C两点，河岸附近还标有D、E、F、B等字母。AC河段位于图中下部到中部一带，C在较低纬度一端，A在较高纬度一端。
推理：题干说明AC之间的河段每年春季会出现凌汛。春季凌汛通常说明河流由较低纬度流向较高纬度，因此该河段流向可判断为从C流向A。面向下游，即从C看向A时，河流左岸为受地转偏向力影响较弱、泥沙堆积较显著的一侧；图中符合的标注河岸为D岸和E岸。按字母顺序排列为D岸、E岸，所以第二处为E岸。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route uses the spring 凌汛 clue to infer downstream direction and then applies the Northern Hemisphere deflection/left-bank deposition rule. It is distinct because the decisive bridge is climatic-hydrologic plus Coriolis bank asymmetry, not simply identifying inner bends by shape.
planner_metadata.image_role: From the image, read that the map is in the Northern Hemisphere near 50°N, that point A lies north/upstream-looking relative to point C on the AC river reach, and locate the named banks D、E、F、B along the channel between C and A. planner_metadata.text_role: Use the statement that the AC reach has spring 凌汛 and the instruction to give the second bank name in alphabetical order.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In the Northern Hemisphere, spring 凌汛 commonly occurs on river reaches flowing from lower latitude to higher latitude because upstream/southern ice thaws first while downstream/northern ice remains frozen. Sort the depositional banks alphabetically.
